## How to Choose the Best Iron Supplement for Anemia  
The right iron supplement for anemia depends on the severity of your deficiency. Mild anemia (ferritin 12–30 ng/mL) often responds well to 18–25 mg of chelated iron daily. Moderate to severe anemia (ferritin below 12 ng/mL) typically requires 45–65 mg of elemental iron under medical supervision. Your doctor can determine the right dose based on your blood work, including ferritin, serum iron, and hemoglobin levels.  
Iron form matters significantly for anemia treatment because you need consistent daily supplementation for 2–3 months. If your supplement causes constipation or nausea, you’re likely to stop taking it before your stores are replenished. Iron bisglycinate causes the fewest side effects while still absorbing well. Ferrous sulfate provides more elemental iron per dose but has higher rates of GI complaints. Heme iron from animal sources absorbs the best but isn’t available in vegan products.  
Always take iron with Vitamin C and away from calcium, coffee, tea, and dairy. Consider whether your anemia is caused by iron deficiency alone or combined with B12 or folate deficiency — a supplement that includes all three nutrients can address multiple deficiency types simultaneously. Get retested after 3 months to confirm your levels are improving, and continue supplementation for as long as your healthcare provider recommends.
